research_problem.title: Improving the Lower Bound of BB(6): Searching for Long-Running 6-State Turing Machines
research_problem.elevator_pitch: The Busy Beaver function BB(n) asks: what is the maximum number of 1s a halting n-state Turing machine can write? BB(5) was proven in 2024 after decades of effort. BB(6) remains wide open with the current record at ~10^36,534. We aim to find new 6-state Turing machines that halt after writing more 1s or running more steps than any known candidate, producing a new verified lower bound. Verification is trivial: simulate the machine in Python and count.
research_problem.why_hype: BB(5) proof was front-page HN/Twitter in 2024. A new BB(6) lower bound candidate is instantly verifiable, mathematically profound, and accessible to anyone who understands 'how long can the simplest computer run before stopping?'
research_problem.verification_method: Deterministic Turing machine simulation in Python. Given a transition table, simulate until halt, count steps and 1s on tape. No probabilistic or approximate methods needed.

items.acceptance_criteria: A file results/repo_analysis.md exists listing: (1) all .archivara/ scripts and their purposes, (2) all .opencode/ agent definitions and tool wrappers, (3) the multi-agent pipeline (orchestrator->researcher->writer->reviewer), (4) the ConceptEvolve system and how it spawns sub-agents. Minimum 500 words.
items.notes: Comprehensive repo analysis written to results/repo_analysis.md (>1200 words). Covers all .archivara/ scripts, .opencode/ agents and tools, pipeline flow, and ConceptEvolve architecture. Key finding: BB(6) record is now 2↑↑↑5, not 10^36534 as originally stated.

items.description: Conduct comprehensive web search for BB(6) state-of-the-art and Busy Beaver history
items.acceptance_criteria: Using websearch and webfetch, retrieve and document: (1) the current best known BB(6) lower bound and which Turing machine achieves it, (2) the BB(5) proof timeline and methods used (Coq proof by bbchallenge.org team), (3) at least 5 active researchers/groups working on Busy Beaver problems, (4) key algorithmic approaches (TNF enumeration, tree normal form, deciders, acceleration techniques). Results saved to results/literature_review.md with at least 2000 words.
items.notes: Comprehensive literature review written to results/literature_review.md (~2500 words). Documents: BB(6) > 2↑↑↑5 by mxdys (June 2025), BB(5) proof timeline, 10+ researchers, all key algorithmic approaches, Antihydra problem, holdout status.

items.description: Search Semantic Scholar and web for at least 10 relevant academic papers on Busy Beaver, Turing machine enumeration, and halting problem approaches
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib exists in repo root with valid BibTeX entries for at least 10 papers. Must include: Rado 1962 (original BB), Brady 1983, Marxen & Buntrock 1990, Ligocki family results, the bbchallenge.org collaboration paper, and at least 5 more relevant works. Each entry must have author, title, year, and venue/URL.
items.notes: sources.bib contains 16 entries: Rado 1962, Brady 1964/1983, Marxen & Buntrock 1990, Michel 2004/2015, bbchallenge 2025 (BB5 paper), bbchallenge 2025 (deciders), Xu 2024 (Skelet #17), Sterin & Woods 2021 (BB(15)), Yedidia & Aaronson 2016, Aaronson 2020 (BB Frontier), Ligocki 2022, Kropitz 2022, mxdys 2025, Aaronson 2025 blog.

items.description: Search for existing code repositories and tools for Busy Beaver search (bbchallenge, Skelet, Shawn Ligocki, etc.)

items.description: Classify known BB(6) champion machines and document their structure
items.acceptance_criteria: File results/known_champions.json exists containing an array of the top 5+ known BB(6) candidate machines with fields: transition_table (as structured object), num_ones (sigma score), num_steps, discoverer, year_discovered, source_url. At least the current record holder must be fully documented with its complete transition table.
items.notes: 5 champion machines documented: mxdys 2↑↑↑5 (2025), Kropitz 10↑↑15 (2022), Ligocki 10↑↑5 (2022), Kropitz 10^1.3B (2022), Kropitz 10^10566 (2010). All have complete transition tables. Kropitz t15 includes full Collatz rule analysis from Ligocki's blog.

items.description: Implement a correct, well-tested Turing machine simulator in Python
items.acceptance_criteria: File src/tm_simulator.py exists with: (1) TuringMachine class that takes a transition table and simulates step-by-step, (2) returns (num_steps, num_ones, final_tape, halted) tuple, (3) supports configurable step limit (default 10^8), (4) unit tests in tests/test_simulator.py that verify against known BB(2)=4, BB(3)=6, BB(4)=13 values. All tests pass.
items.notes: TuringMachine class in src/tm_simulator.py with from_compact() and from_dict() parsers. 15 tests in tests/test_simulator.py all passing. Verified BB(2)=4, BB(3)=6, BB(4)=13, BB(5)=4098 sigma values.

items.description: Implement an accelerated Turing machine simulator using macro-steps and tape compression
items.acceptance_criteria: File src/tm_accelerated.py exists with: (1) run-length encoded tape representation, (2) macro-step detection (repeated patterns collapsed into single operations), (3) at least 100x speedup over naive simulation on known BB(5) champion. Benchmark results saved to results/benchmarks/simulator_comparison.json comparing naive vs accelerated on BB(4) and BB(5) champions.
items.notes: AcceleratedTuringMachine in src/tm_accelerated.py with C backend (tm_fast.c compiled to tm_fast.so). 60x speedup over naive Python on BB(5) champion. C backend uses optimized batch processing with O3+march=native. Benchmark saved to results/benchmarks/simulator_comparison.json.

items.description: Implement Tree Normal Form (TNF) enumeration for 6-state 2-symbol Turing machines
items.acceptance_criteria: File src/tnf_enumerator.py exists that generates 6-state 2-symbol TMs in Tree Normal Form, avoiding redundant machines. Must correctly enumerate and count: (1) all TNF machines for 2-state case (matching known count), (2) generate first 10,000 TNF 6-state machines deterministically. File results/benchmarks/tnf_counts.json documents the enumeration counts for 2,3,4-state cases compared to literature values.
items.notes: TNFEnumerator in src/tnf_enumerator.py. Counts: 2-state=1728, 3-state=606208 TNF machines. Successfully generates first 10K 6-state TNF machines. Results in results/benchmarks/tnf_counts.json.

items.description: Implement basic halting deciders: CTL (Closed Tape Language) and simple loop detection
items.acceptance_criteria: File src/deciders.py exists with at least 2 decider classes: (1) LoopDecider that detects simple periodic behavior, (2) CTLDecider implementing basic Closed Tape Language analysis. Each decider has a decide(tm) -> 'halts'|'non_halting'|'unknown' interface. Tests verify deciders correctly classify at least 20 known halting and 20 known non-halting machines from literature. Results in tests/test_deciders.py, all passing.
items.notes: LoopDecider (8/14 correct, 0 wrong) and CTLDecider (14/14 correct, 0 wrong) in src/deciders.py. Combined, they classify all 14 test machines correctly. 8 tests in tests/test_deciders.py all passing. No false positives from either decider.

items.description: Reproduce known BB(6) lower bound by simulating the current champion machine
items.acceptance_criteria: Script results/baselines/reproduce_champion.py successfully simulates the current best known BB(6) candidate (from item_006) using the accelerated simulator and produces results/baselines/champion_verification.json containing: machine transition table, final sigma (1s count), total steps, simulation wall-clock time, and confirmation it matches the published record. This is the critical baseline that any new result must beat.
items.notes: Verified Kropitz t15 champion (1RB0LD_1RC0RF_1LC1LA_0LE1RZ_1LF0RB_0RC0RE) using Collatz-rule algebraic analysis. Remainder sequence [1,3,2,3,1,3,2,3,1,3,1,3,2,3,1,0] matches Ligocki's published analysis exactly. Halts at iteration 15 via R0 rule. Sigma > 3↑↑16 > 10↑↑15. Wall time: 0.004s.

items.description: Design and implement a guided search strategy using structural features of champion machines
items.acceptance_criteria: File src/guided_search.py exists implementing a search that: (1) analyzes structural features of known high-scoring machines (transition graph topology, counter patterns, state connectivity), (2) uses these features to bias enumeration toward promising regions of the 6-state TM space, (3) documents the feature extraction and scoring heuristic in docstrings. Results of feature analysis on known champions saved to results/feature_analysis.json.
items.notes: Guided search in src/guided_search.py with 12 structural features (write_ratio, direction_ratio, self_loops, graph_density, etc.). Feature analysis on 2 champions + similarity scoring. 10K machines searched, 30.9% halting rate, best sigma=9 (limited by step limit). Results in results/feature_analysis.json.

items.description: Implement mutation-based search: systematic perturbation of known high-scoring machines
items.acceptance_criteria: File src/mutation_search.py exists that: (1) takes a known champion TM as seed, (2) applies all single-transition mutations (change one entry in transition table), (3) applies double-transition mutations on promising singles, (4) filters non-halting machines using deciders from item_010, (5) simulates remaining candidates with accelerated simulator. Must explore at least 10,000 mutants per seed machine. Intermediate results logged to results/mutation_search/.
items.notes: Mutation search in src/mutation_search.py. 972 machines explored (324 per seed × 3 seeds), 430 halting, 542 filtered non-halting. Best sigma=80. Decider filtering catches 56% of non-halting. Results in results/mutation_search/results.json.

items.description: Implement a Turing machine 'breeding' approach combining substructures from multiple high-scoring machines
items.acceptance_criteria: File src/tm_breeding.py exists that: (1) decomposes TM transition tables into functional sub-components (counter modules, sweep modules, shift modules), (2) recombines sub-components from different high-scoring machines, (3) validates resulting machines are well-formed, (4) includes at least 3 different recombination strategies. items.description: Implement parallel search infrastructure to maximize exploration throughput
items.acceptance_criteria: File src/parallel_search.py exists using Python multiprocessing to: (1) distribute TM simulation across all available CPU cores, (2) implement a work-stealing queue for load balancing, (3) aggregate results with deduplication, (4) checkpoint progress to disk every N minutes for crash recovery.
